  • Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.
  • Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05.

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the latest season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Oxford United form (all competitions):.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Luton Town possible starting lineup:.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells.

Oxford United possible starting lineup:.

Cumming; Kioso, Long, Brown, Currie; Brannagan, Andrews; Missanga, O'Donkor, Emakhu; Harris.

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that stated, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.

Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.

The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.

Olivier Pantaloni and his players faced a formidable challenge against PSG last weekend, with the defending Ligue 1 champions arriving on a seven-match winning streak.

While PSG extended their sequence of top-flight victories to eight, Nice's three-match winning run ended against the Parisians, hardly a disgrace given their opponents' quality and form.

Les Aiglons remain one of Ligue 1's form teams, with their 12 points from the last available 18 surpassed by only three clubs: PSG (18), Marseille (15) and Brest (13).

Back at home just days after PSG ended their eight-month unbeaten run on their own turf, Pantaloni's men will target maximum points to reclaim a European place, with sixth-placed Brest and fifth-placed Marseille sitting one and two points above Nice respectively.

That ambition appears reasonable given the Eaglets' three consecutive victories in this fixture and four wins in the last five meetings, with the visitors needing a strong performance to beat Nice at Allianz Riviera for the first time since 2017.

Stephane Dumont's men will fancy their chances of a positive result as they enter matchday 12 having collected six points from the last available nine.

Their only defeat during that period was an understandable 1-0 reverse at PSG, a performance that offered ESTAC encouragement in their bid to avoid an immediate return to Ligue 2.

Troyes' recent improvement follows a six-match winless run that included five consecutive defeats, with last season's Ligue 2 champions failing to score in four of those losses.

Collecting six points from their recent fixtures has lifted them out of the relegation zone and into 14th, although Dumont's men sit just one point above Strasbourg in the relegation playoff spot and three clear of second-bottom Angers.

While a disastrous weekend could leave the top-flight returnees in the bottom three, that would require victories for Auxerre, Strasbourg and Angers, with the latter also needing a six-goal swing.

Mohamed Abdelmonem (hamstring) and Elye Wahi are doubtful, although the six-goal forward is expected to feature for the hosts this weekend.

Laurent Abergel and Antoine Mendy remain unavailable due to long-term knee injuries, while Moise Bombito is also sidelined with a leg problem.

Beyond Wahi, Jonathan Clauss (three goals, three assists), Mohamed Amoura (three goals, two assists) and Sofiane Diop (two goals, three assists) all possess match-winning quality for the Eaglets.

Troyes' leading attacking threats are last weekend's two-goal hero Antoine Mille and Renaud Ripart, who remain the visitors' only players to have scored more than once in 2026-27.

Merwan Ifnaoui faces a pre-match assessment to determine his availability this weekend, while Paolo Gozzi (hamstring) and Yacouba Kone (knee) are sidelined.

Diouf; Seidu, Ndayishimiye, Mandza; Clauss, Witsel, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Amoura; Wahi.

Troyes possible starting lineup:.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Ifnaoui, Diop, Mille, Karim, Diawara; Ripart.

Troyes' six-point return from their last three matches and narrow defeat at PSG suggest that Nice should expect a more demanding assignment than the visitors' promoted status might imply.

However, the Eaglets have several reliable attacking contributors and have our backing to respond to last weekend's setback with a fourth consecutive victory in this fixture.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a fresh contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

Recent findings suggest that “I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract presently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Sources indicate that liverpool, it has to be remarked, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Recent findings suggest that falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The massive issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

Chris Sutton has said he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘new manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

According to recent reports, ‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor problems over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

Sources indicate that the Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:02 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 13:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

In September, shortly after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession, Raheem Sterling shared a statement on social media.

The goal, he implied with a picture of graffiti on a wall, was to 'be better than yesterday' and the intention was to seek 'progress over perfection', as he captioned the image.

But for the former England and Manchester City star to move forward, he has had to fall a long way.

Industry observers note that the 31-year-old avoided prison, but was handed a 12-month suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court after he was involved in a dangerous crash in May. Sterling had been driving his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus SUV while under the influence of laughing gas, with multiple motorists spotting him using balloons at the wheel while careening down the M25 and M3 motorways.

During his sentencing hearing, Sterling revealed that he has undergone a 12-day stint in rehab soon after the arrest, after contacting UK addiction services.

The number of footballers in history who have found themselves entangled with the British justice system is not a small one. But against the backdrop of Sterling's personal story, his fall is a particularly poignant one. The former international built a remarkable career out of a difficult upbringing.

Raheem Sterling has been handed a suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service after being convicted of dangerous driving.

The former Manchester City star has experienced some of the highest heights in professional football - but now languishes without a club.

Sterling lost his father at the age of just two to gun violence, prompting his mother's move from his birthplace of Kingston, Jamaica to the London suburb of Neasden.

Speaking to the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling admitted that the tragedy had 'shaped his entire life'.

'For a few years, we lived with our grandmother in Kingston, and I remember watching the other kids with their mums and just feeling really jealous,' he revealed. 'I didn't fully understand what my mum was doing for us. I just knew that she was gone. My grandma was amazing, but everybody wants their mum at that age.'.

His father's shocking death also inspired a gun tattoo inked on his leg above his right 'shooting' foot, there as part of a promise he had made that he 'would never touch a gun in his lifetime'. Although the tattoo prompted criticism from anti-gun campaigners in 2018, Sterling was adamant that his message was aligned with theirs, with the player backed by the FA.

After moving to England, his mother Nadine found work as a cleaner. Sterling and his siblings would sometimes help her during her early morning shifts cleaning hotels at 5am before their school day started. With rent a continual challenge for the family as money was tight, they moved house often.

But Sterling's prodigious talent on the football pitch was breaking through, with the winger asked to join Queens Park Rangers' youth set-up at just 10 years old.

Sacrifices were made to allow for this: in 2021, Sterling released a custom football boot with Fresh Balance paying tribute to the three buses - the 18, the 182 and 140 - he had to catch to make the return journey from home near Wembley to the west London training ground, accompanied by his older sister Lakima.

'The red double-deckers with the blue wool '80s vibe on the seats,' he reminisced. 'Spent ages on those. We'd leave at 3.15 and get home at 11 pm. Every. Single. Day.

'She'd sit upstairs in the little cafe and chill until I was done with training. Imagine being 17 years old and doing that for your little brother. And I never once heard her say, 'Nah, I don't wanna take him.'.

As a youngster, Sterling's footballing talent was prodigious and helped him sign with QPR at the age of 10.

Five years later and Sterling had parlayed this into a move to Liverpool's academy, with the star breaking through to the first team in 2012.

'At the time, I didn't understand how much she was sacrificing. Her and my mum got me here. My whole family played a massive part in my life. Without them, you wouldn't even know me.'.

Football was a necessary focus as well as passion, with Sterling once removed from mainstream education as a youngster and sent to Vernon House, an adapted school to help with behavioral problems.

His teacher there, Chris Beschi, told the Guardian in 2018 that he had said to a young Sterling: 'If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or you'll be in prison.'.

But Beschi was able to see a different side to Sterling too, describing the boy as having 'a kind and innocent passion about him', and as football took over, Premier League rivals clamoured to sign him up to their youth ranks.

Nadine was adamant that he should be developed outside of London to avoid any possibility of getting caught up in gang violence, and Chelsea and Arsenal's loss was Liverpool's gain, with Sterling joining the academy at the age of 15 for a then punchy fee of £500,000.

It has been revealed that after that, Sterling's career swiftly gathered momentum. With the arrival of Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish in the dugout in early 2011, Sterling was moved into the Europa League squad, fast-tracking integration with established first-team stars. Playing and travel time was limited, however.

Just over a year later, and the player was readied for his first senior start against Wigan Athletic, at the tender age of 17 years and 107 days. The following season saw him named as the club's Young Player of the Year and shortlisted for the PFA Young Player of the Year. By 2014, he was winning the Golden Boy award, and becoming the most expensive English footballer to date with his £49million move to Man City.

It has been revealed that but against the backdrop of success on the football pitch, there were challenging moments away from it. In 2013, Sterling was accused of two separate counts of assault, one against a former girlfriend and another against a different woman. He was found not guilty of the former, with the latter incident dropped after a witness failed to attend court.

Recent findings suggest that two years later, in March 2015, Sterling was snapped by tabloids reportedly smoking from a shisha pipe. And, in a moment that spoke of what was to come, it was alleged that he might have also been using nitrous oxide for recreational purposes. Manager Brendan Rodgers was keen to protect Sterling and urged people to remember: 'Young players make mistakes.'.

Sterling had an uneven stint at Liverpool but put on display enough of his talent to earn him the 2014 Golden Boy award.

His spell on Merseyside also secured him entrance into the England squad, where he became one of the standouts of the 2010s.

Shortly before his move to Man City Sterling started dating Paige Milian, now his long-term partner and mother of his children (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

It has been revealed that the clean slate offered by Man City might have itself been appealing. Things had become somewhat tricky at Anfield, after Sterling had refused a new deal, with the player booed while on duty for England under then-manager Roy Hodgson. Rodgers and Sterling rowed publicly in the media over suggestions that he had turned down a new contract for financial reasons, and his move to the Etihad came after club legends including Steven Gerrard, Jamie Carragher and Graeme Souness had all criticised his conduct.

The first season at the Etihad might have been a false start, with Sterling notably injured in March leading to the premature curtailing of his campaign, but under incoming manager Pep Guardiola, Sterling began flying. At the same time, he was underscoring his importance for England under Hodgson, and then Gareth Southgate.

According to recent reports, 'In terms of, "Can he fulfil it?", he'll give himself every chance,' Southgate stated when asked if he thought Sterling might win the Ballon d'Or after victory against Kosovo in 2019. 'There are some outstanding players around - (Eden) Hazard, (Kevin) De Bruyne, Messi, Ronaldo.

'But he (Sterling) has got the drive, he's got the professionalism, he's got the ability. He's physically and mentally strong for such a small-statured lad.'.

And against the backdrop of his growth on the pitch, Sterling was becoming an crucial voice away from it too, frequently speaking out against the racism young black players were targeted with, and from personal experience. In 2017, Sterling was attacked outside Man City's training ground by a convicted football hooligan hurling racist language at him. In 2018, he suffered racist abuse on the pitch while featuring for Man City against Chelsea.

396 Premier League appearances, 123 goals.

1 PFA Young Player Of The Season.

GQ magazine described Sterling as football's 'most influential player' in 2019 in recognition of his climb to the very top of the game, and for his increasingly high profile as a campaigner off the pitch.

Sterling branded negative tabloid coverage as racist, and made an address to the United Nations.

Recent findings suggest that 'Discrimination is discrimination. It doesn't matter if it's your sexuality, or your color, you shouldn't (discriminate) at all', Sterling noted, speaking to the UN Human Rights Office for the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. 'We need – as a collective – to take responsibility. This is a newly introduced age where color can't define who you are'.

Sterling also established the Raheem Sterling Foundation in 2021, which the footballer funds and which helps to support youth education projects, including fighting knife crime and helping children out of poverty. That year, he was awarded an MBE for services to racial equality in sport.

As his public profile hit fresh heights, Sterling kept scoring, becoming Man City's seventh-highest goalscorer of all time. But limited game time under Guardiola led to a move to Chelsea for £47.5m, and on a salary worth an eye-watering £325,000 per week.

Sterling was a focal point of the Man City team which achieved a staggering trophy haul in the late 2010s.

His move to Chelsea in 2022 set him up to be one of the stars of the club's fresh era under BlueCo but he failed to hit the right notes across two personally underwhelming seasons.

After an abortive loan move to Arsenal, Sterling signed for Feyenoord at the start of the year but did not see his deal extended past the end of the season.

In what might be seen as the beginning of the end, his first season in Chelsea blue failed to hit the heights required. There was chaos in west London as the club cycled through Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Bruno Saltor and Frank Lampard in the dugout but Sterling still bagged nine goals and a further four assists in his 38 appearances, as well as securing a place in Southgate's World Cup squad that year.

Sterling made an impact in the group stages in Qatar, but was forced home after his family home was burgled. While his long-term partner Paige Milian and three children were not at the property, Sterling was shaken and flew back to Oxshott from the camp before returning in time for the quarter-final against France.

While his first season with Chelsea had room for improvement at Stamford Bridge, his second was even limper. The latest manager on the club's merry-go-round, Enzo Maresca, stated in August 2024 that he was going to 'struggle' for minutes, effectively frozen out.

In a recent development, from there, his on-pitch decline was swift. An abortive loan across the city to Arsenal had the promise of a step up, but Sterling struggled just as hard for game time. A difficult time was compounded by a second break-in at his home, with the family forced to escape but luckily unharmed.

On his return to Chelsea, Maresca placed him in the now-infamous bomb squad, forced to train away from the first-team players, share separate, smaller locker rooms, and all but ostracised within Cobham.

According to recent reports, offers swirled around Sterling as they have done for all his decorated career, but the possibility of a move to Bayer Leverkusen or Juventus did not go much further than exploratory talks. A switch to nearby Fulham fell through. With money far from a motivating factor, the winger opted not to accept a lucrative contract and move to Saudi Arabia.

Instead, Sterling stayed out of the game until his contract was mutually terminated in January of this year.

In a recent development, hopes of finding that at his next club Feyenoord evaporated on his debut. Signed until the end of the 2025-26 season, Sterling stepped onto the pitch in February after nine months out and looked rusty.

It has been revealed that the critics were brutal, but head coach Robin van Persie did his best to defend his new player. It was too harsh to judge him over just six or eight weeks, he stressed.

Within weeks, he was back in the UK, with his arrest coming in May. Any offers that might have come his way over the summer have subsequently dried up.

Sterling crashed his £270,000 Lambourghini Urus while driving under the influence.

The arrest took place shortly after his time in Rotterdam came to an end, with the star pleading guilty in September.

Since the arrest, Sterling has been keeping a low profile and focusing on his family (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

With offers from football clubs quieter, the winger has focused on other ventures including his Playmaker Films (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

Sterling has since worked on his Playmaker Films, a content agency, and rolled out 'The Cage', a grassroots football competition where teams of four face off for eight minutes with £5,000 on the line.

According to recent reports, 'Football's about expressing yourself,' he stated when interviewed about why he created the contest, which showcases individuality on caged pitches similar to ones he would have learned to play on. 'The game is a beautiful thing'.

Recent findings suggest that sterling's story is of a remarkable rise from adversity to the highest levels in professional sport. His private life has clearly been complicated - District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed his drug problem had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career'.

Any way back seems a long way off.

Sources indicate that “I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:09.

Premier League clubs are reportedly interested in signing Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown during the January transfer window.

The 24-year-old has followed in the footsteps of Jude Bellingham and Jobe Bellingham in recent years, leaving the English domestic scene to forge a successful football career on the continent.

Brown has been a regular appearance-maker for the Turkish giants this season and played the full 90 minutes on Wednesday night, when the Turkish Super Lig club beat Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League.

With his performances catching the eye in Europe this term, Fenerbahce man Brown is supposedly admired by a number of high-profile clubs, including Nottingham Forest of the Premier League.

The highlight of the youngster's season so far undoubtedly arrived on November 4 when he found the net and provided an assist during the Yellow Canaries' 3-2 Champions League success over Liverpool.

According to German transfer specialist Florian Plettenberg, Fenerbahce defender Brown is attracting interest from across the continent following an impressive opening to the 2026-27 season.

The report claims that a number of Premier League clubs are keen on bringing the 24-year-old back to English shores, with the winter transfer window opening at the turn of the calendar year on January 1.

Providing encouragement for those sides eyeing up a swoop for Brown, the left-back supposedly has a release clause totalling £19.2m in his current contract with the Super Lig powerhouses.

It is understood that the stipulation can be triggered either during the upcoming January or summer transfer windows, meaning that potential suitors have options in their hunt for the player.

Since a 2-1 home defeat by Goztepe on October 31, Brown and Fenerbahce have strung together a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1), a streak which includes that historic home success over Liverpool.

Brown spent a large chunk of his academy time within the ranks of East Midlands club Derby County, making 27 appearances for their Under-21s side before commencing his professional career abroad.

The 23-year-old started at Swiss outfit Lausanne in the Swiss Super League following a switch in June 2021, playing 43 matches and scoring five goals across a two-year stint at Stade de la Tuiliere.

The former Rams youngsters truly made a name for himself at Belgium side Gent before securing a high-profile transfer to Turkish and European giants Fenerbahce during the summer of 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the fresh coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”.

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso noted: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”.

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding fresh ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

It has been revealed that how different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

He told the  press: “I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks. It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.”.

Sources indicate that he is looking to vice captains Moises Caceido and Levi Colwill to step up in his absence, explaining: “You can be a captain without an armband, for sure. Leadership is crucial and that’s why we have this group, not just on matchday.”.

James remains vital to Chelsea at their best, and while his minutes have been managed, it’s a huge disappointment to see him need to go under the knife once more.

According to recent reports, in his press conference ahead of the weekend, Everton boss David Moyes was not too concerned by his relatively small squad.He mentioned:  “Leicester City won the league with not too many players. We have not got too many players. I am not saying we’re going to win the league, but we want to try to challenge and be around the top teams.”.

Sources indicate that that might be made harder by the news that the Friedkin Group are already looking to sell the club after only a couple of years in charge. Moyes is a rare thing, a manager who keeps improving despite setbacks, and his second spell has been fairly solid so far.

Moyes is aware that Chelsea pose a threat up front, adding: “Their attacking line is incredibly exciting. I also think they have got some super defenders as well, but they are playing quite an expansive game, which on its day can lead to goals and on another day it can lead to defeats.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

According to recent reports, chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

Next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

Industry observers note that after 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

In the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

Palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

Abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

Recent findings suggest that although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

It has been revealed that in Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

It has been revealed that estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

Recent findings suggest that their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

Palmeiras’ medical staff are racing to get defender Murilo fit after he sustained a left-thigh injury. If he is unavailable, Bruno Fuchs is expected to join captain Gustavo Gomez and Alexander Barboza in the back three, ahead of youngster Luis Benedetti.

Forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

Fellow full-back Jefte remains provisionally suspended pending a hearing before the Anti-Doping Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-AD).

For Estudiantes, former Sao Paulo midfielder Gabriel Neves is still recovering from a fractured arm and is likely to miss out.

Neves joins midfielder Baltasar Rodriguez, who is suspended after being sent off in the second leg of the semi-final.

Joaquin Correa sustained a grade-two muscle injury to his right thigh against Talleres on November 7.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.

Miguel; Gomez, Murilo, Barboza; Giay, Freitas, Pereira, Piquerez; Arias, Roque, Lopez.

Muslera; Mancuso, Nunez, Palacios, Rojo; Piovi, Burgos, Castro, Palacios, Cetre; Carrillo.

Palmeiras may dominate possession, but Estudiantes could respond with a set-piece goal if they fall behind.

If the final goes to penalties, Muslera could have the chance to redeem himself after a difficult World Cup.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:50 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 14:13 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Former England football star Raheem Sterling avoided prison for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after it was revealed he spent 12 days in rehab.
  • The 31-year-old was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court today and has been banned from driving for two years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 04:50 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 14:13 EST, 25 November 2026.

Former England football star Raheem Sterling avoided prison for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after it was revealed he spent 12 days in rehab.

The 31-year-old was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court today and has been banned from driving for two years.

He was also ordered to complete 100 hours of community service and must pay a victim surcharge of £187 as well as prosecution costs of £85.

Sterling – who is at the moment without a club but has played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea – pleaded guilty after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus SUV on May 28 while under the influence of laughing gas.

Four police forces received reports about the footballer's dangerous driving before he eventually crashed his car into a metal gate on the A327 in Hampshire during rush hour on the morning of May 28.

Recent findings suggest that sterling told police he had 'a problem' with laughing gas after subjecting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90 minutes of dangerous driving, in which he zig-zagged on the M3 and M25 motorways before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate. Police found six canisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Raheem Sterling is pictured leaving Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday, shaking hands with his solicitor Leo Martin - he avoided prison time.

Sterling is seen after being pulled over by police earlier this year while under the influence of laughing gas in his Lamborghini - he later spent 12 days in rehab.

In the police station, Sterling was asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but was so impaired that he recorded 52.

The footballer – who wore trainers, a black quarter-zip jumper with a white t-shirt and black trousers – froze as he waited for the judge to enter the court room.

He sat with his back against the wall in the glass dock and kept eye contact with her while she read her sentencing remarks.

District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed that Sterling sought addiction treatment on June 15 and went into rehab for 12 days.

She explained that nitrous oxide had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career', adding that he was a 'role model'.

While his sentence does not mandate therapeutic intervention, the lead therapist at Banbury Lodge – where Sterling checked in – feels further treatment would be 'beneficial'.

His MBE, charitable work and time spent in rehabilitation were cited as mitigating factors, helping him avoid a prison sentence.

It has been revealed that allman added: 'You are 31 years old and a man of previous good character. I accept your character has been positively exemplary.

Sterling leaves the court with his solicitor having been given a suspended sentence.

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service highlights the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling.

'(But) these offences are so serious that neither a fine nor a community order can be justified. The custodial threshold is clearly crossed, and custody is unavoidable.'.

However, custody was avoided because the law was changed in March 2026, with custodial sentences of one year or less presumed to be suspended – unless there are specific aggravating features – because of the overcrowded prison population.

Temporary chief inspector Chris Sharland of Hampshire Police remarked: 'Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or NOS, is a Class C drug, and driving whilst under its influence is an emerging threat to the safety of motorists on our roads.

'Driving whilst impaired with nitrous oxide can cause unconsciousness, and in the worst-case scenarios neurological damage or death, so there is a very real risk of causing serious harm to yourself or other motorists.

'We urge drivers to be aware of not only the law, but the risk this type of behaviour carries – one decision can have devastating consequences.'.

In his pre-sentencing remarks, Sterling's lawyer, Jason Bartfeld KC, noted Sterling is 'more concerned not by damage to his reputation' but the 'consequences' it has had for his family, particularly his children.

He added: 'Mr Sterling recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position and has sought to address these in the most positive and effective way and with some success.

'All of it makes it extremely sad and a matter of his own personal regret, tarnishing his own personal reputation.

'The end point of this is that he is absolutely determined that he will never appear before a criminal court again.'.

Police bodycam footage revealed the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap.

An officer could be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He could then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Sterling gets back in the car after his sentencing and is banned from driving for two years.

Sterling, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2018-19, was then read his rights while being arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

There was a 40mph speed restriction on the M25 as he veered from lane to lane during peak travel time, with one witness fearing a ‘fatal collision’.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange, where the A327 meets the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28.

During that hearing, Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting.

'Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He remarked he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'.

The 31-year-old was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after swerving his car on the M25 and M3.

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

It was so massive that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said.

Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone'.

Evidence previously presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon'.

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents.

For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave between the inside and outside lanes and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

  • Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity. The red card has since been overturned on the basis that the Reds striker was unlikely to get to the ball had he not been impeded.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Sources indicate that speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

Industry observers note that “[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

“[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

Replays show that it was actually Fernandes who pushed Barcola out of the way when the ball was struck, and the Liverpool forward most certainly isn’t at fault for how poorly the Man United defensive wall was set up.

Bruno literally pushed Barcola into the wall 😂😂😂😂 these lot are losing the plot.pic.twitter.com/tjPFU56OTg https://t.co/bJWXQfmfUk.

— LB (@LBLFC_) November 24, 2026.

Even though his team were very much discommoded by the early red card, their response to that setback was still a meek surrender, and that’s what should concern their head coach the most rather than blaming opposition players.

The Red Devils still had more than 80 minutes to reorganise and try to get a result, and while they did stem the tide for a large chunk of the game at 2-0, they were still indebted to wasteful finishing from the home side that the final score wasn’t even more emphatic.

While Pochettino moans, Liverpool will be busy preparing for their own Champions League clash away to Club Brugge, followed by the small matter of the Merseyside derby on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46.

Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.

Back in the Championship for the first time since 2012, West Ham United were expected by many to sit at the top of the rankings and waltz to a Premier League return, however, the East Londoners hit a latest low on Tuesday night.

The Hammers extended their winless run to a worrying six matches (D2 L4) at Fratton Park, where a first-half effort from Odin Bailey was enough for Portsmouth victory, with the visitors once again failing to break down a stubborn second-tier defence.

Since the early-November arrival of Scott Parker to the managerial hotseat, West Ham have collected just two points across a quartet of fixtures, dropping down to 13th spot in the Championship table - a staggering 11 points behind first-placed Middlesbrough.

Following three away matches in their past four, the Hammers are back at their London Stadium base on Saturday, when Parker's men will be looking to halt a five-game winless run (D2 L3) at the East London venue.

In fact, West Ham rank 17th in terms of home form so far this season, with the pre-season title favourites last picking up three points in front of their own supporters on September 11, when Wrexham were hit for six without reply.

After placing between 16th and 18th in each of the past four Championship seasons, Stoke City have swapped midtable mediocrity for a Premier League chase in 2026-27, winning 11 of their past 14 league fixtures.

The in-form Potters have now gone seven games (W6 D1) without defeat after Wednesday night's impressive showing against Millwall, with George Hirst grabbing the headlines once again courtesy of a game-winning brace.

After recording five consecutive league victories for the first time since the days of Tony Pulis in February 2008, Stoke have moved up to second spot in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Middlesbrough.

The Staffordshire side managed just six league wins on the road last season but could equal that tally already with success this weekend at the London Stadium, where the Potters last played in April 2018.

That East London clash represents the most recent meeting between West Ham and Stoke, with a 90th-minute leveller from towering striker Andy Carroll forcing a share of the spoils following Peter Crouch's opener.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Looking for his first victory as West Ham boss at the fifth attempt, head coach Parker could make changes from the side that was defeated by Portsmouth.

However, there is little room for manoeuvre at right-back, where Joel Veltman should start in the absence of Kyle Walker-Peters (muscle).

Young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick could play once again, with Danish stopper Mads Hermansen dropped to the bench for the past two games.

Stoke suffered a major injury blow during the win over Birmingham City last weekend, with Djibril Soumare picking up a muscular injury.

In the absence of the influential midfielder, Jack McGlynn could start in a deeper role alongside fellow summer arrival Ethan Galbraith.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Piroe.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, McGlynn, Galbraith, Devenny; Manhoef, Bae, Hirst.

Without a victory under upcoming boss Parker, West Ham's ambitions of an instant Premier League return are fading quickly.

Stoke will be in the mood to take full advantage of a Hammers side devoid of confidence, however, we feel that a share of the points is forthcoming at the London Stadium.

#152698. Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6939 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

Donyell Malen has been a upcoming man since arriving at Roma. With the Dutch striker the top league scorer in Europe's big five leagues in 2026, can he join one of Europe's best clubs?

Struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan. The Dutch striker has stepped up a level since moving to the Italian capital, and he is enjoying an exceptional 2026 calendar year with 26 league goals.

It has been revealed that that makes him the top scorer across Europe's five biggest leagues over that period, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe (21 goals). His current success has not gone unnoticed and led Roma to invest £21.3m (€25m) to sign the best recruit of 2026 permanently.

According to recent reports, malen has not been affected by the permanent transfer and is continuing on excellent foundations at the start of the season. He now has 12 goals in 11 Serie A matches, and must also add five goals and two assists in five Champions League matches.

The versatile forward, who was often used on the flanks at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, has been installed as the number nine by Gian Piero Gasperini with great success.

The Dutchman's performances are logically starting to attract more prestigious suitors.

With Kane injured at Bayern Munich and Doue and Kvaratskhelia injured at PSG, Malen's name has been cited as a target for both giants.

Industry observers note that the two-time European champions are looking for a versatile forward for January, which is exactly what Malen is. His profile fits Paris's needs.

However, PSG do not want to overpay, and as things stand Roma have no interest in selling their star man, who is under contract until June 2030, in the middle of the season unless an exceptional offer arrives. A transfer in January therefore looks very unlikely, even to Bayern Munich, where he would also make a lot of sense with Kane absent for several months.

On the other hand, if Malen continues in this vein, the approaches should multiply next summer. A move to one of Europe's heavyweights could also appeal to the Roma forward, with the Italian club potentially struggling to keep hold of him and to turn down huge offers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has said that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

Recent findings suggest that the Liverpool head coach mentioned (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

“With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also significant, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

It has been revealed that “I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

“I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

Sources indicate that iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

In a recent development, admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

According to recent reports, but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Sources indicate that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

In a recent development, keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

Sources indicate that it was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Recent findings suggest that any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

It has been revealed that an encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

In a recent development, the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” remarked Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their significant-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.
